communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: LIHTC Detroit
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Properties located within the City of Detroit that have received, been allocated, reserved or otherwise been associated with Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, including federal 9% credits and 4% credits.

For each LIHTC project located in Detroit, please provide the following information, if maintained:

- Project name and any prior or alternate project names
- Complete street address and ZIP code
- Project identification number, application number or allocation number
- Current owner name
- General partner, managing member, developer, sponsor or affiliated entity names
- Number of total residential units
- Number of LIHTC-restricted units
- Credit type, including 9% credits, 4% credits or other applicable category
- Date of allocation, reservation, award, placed-in-service date or other relevant program date
- Credit allocation amount or annual credit amount, if available
- Current compliance or extended-use status, if maintained
- Any recorded expiration, termination, foreclosure, transfer, ownership-change or other status information concerning the project’s LIHTC restrictions

If MSHDA maintains a master list, project inventory, allocation list, compliance database, or similar report containing this information, please provide that record rather than requiring the information to be compiled manually.

The requested time period is from the beginning of the LIHTC program through the date this request is processed. If a full historical search is not reasonably available, please provide the complete records currently maintained by MSHDA and identify the earliest date covered by those records.

This request seeks existing public records and does not require MSHDA to create a new record or answer questions. If the requested information is maintained in multiple records, please provide the records in the form in which they are ordinarily maintained.

If MSHDA determines that the request is too broad or needs clarification, please identify the specific concern and provide an opportunity to narrow or clarify the request before denying it.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Aaron Mondry

title: Clinton Presidential Library: Visitor & Protocol Records for Günter Straßmeir ("Günter Strassmeir")

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Clinton Presidential Library: Visitor & Protocol Records for Günter Straßmeir ("Günter Strassmeir")
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552) and the Presidential Records Act (44 U.S.C. § 2201 et seq.), I hereby request access to all textual records, visitor entry logs, protocol lists, and event rosters referring or relating to:

SUBJECT INDIVIDUAL: 

Günter Straßmeir (transliterations: Gunter Strassmeir, Gunter Strassmeier, Gunther Strassmeir; DOB: June 20, 1929 – DOD: December 24, 2009), former Parliamentary State Secretary to Chancellor Helmut Kohl and member of the Berlin House of Representatives. 

For guidance, here's the German Wikipedia entry: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%BCnter_Stra%C3%9Fmeir Strassmeir was a close confidant and former chief of staff to Helmut Kohl. 

SPECIFIC SCOPE & RECORD GROUPS:

White House Visitor Records / WAVES Logs (or predecessor/functional-equivalent system): Any record of entry, scheduled appointment, or security clearance pass for Günter Straßmeir attending meetings, receptions, or bilateral briefings at the White House complex, for the full period January 20, 1993, through January 20, 1997 [see note below].

Office of Public Liaison / Foreign Delegation Files: Roster lists, participant schedules, or background materials mentioning Günter Straßmeir in connection with German-American parliamentary exchanges, Congress-Bundestag seminars, or CDU delegation visits to Washington, D.C., specifically surrounding the dates of March 26, 1993, and January 31, 1994.

White House Social Office: Guest lists and seating charts for events surrounding the visits of German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on March 26, 1993, and January 31, 1994.

If any responsive records are withheld in whole or in part, I request that you identify each withheld document individually (a Vaughn index) and specify the FOIA exemption or PRA restriction applied to it. For any records withheld as currently and properly classified, I invoke the mandatory declassification review process under Executive Order 13526, Section 3.5, and request that this letter serve as an MDR request in the alternative.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request existing records held by your concerning OCR case [08231455] and its associated resolution agreement(s). The time period is from Jan 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed.

Please provide the following existing records, in native electronic format where available:

1. Correspondence between District personnel, agents, counsel, or contractors and the U.S. Department of Education Office for Civil Rights (OCR) concerning the case, agreement, monitoring, implementation, reporting, modification, closure, or any deliverable.

2. Any bounced, undeliverable, rejected, failed-delivery, out-of-office, automated-reply, or other message indicating an attempted OCR contact did not reach the intended recipient or did not receive a substantive response.

3. Records submitted, prepared for submission, or maintained for submission to OCR, including reports, data, policies, training materials, remediation records, implementation updates, requests for approval, and records identifying deliverables that remain outstanding.

4. OCR acknowledgments, questions, feedback, approvals, rejections, requested revisions, extensions, status updates, or other responses to District submissions.

5. Internal District communications that discuss inability to reach OCR; delayed, missing, or unresolved OCR feedback or approval; whether the District considered an agreement obligation complete without OCR approval; or whether an individual student remedy, compensatory service, training, policy change, survey, reporting requirement, or other systemwide change was delayed.

6. Existing logs, trackers, calendars, transmittal records, meeting notes, or similar records sufficient to show, for each submission to OCR: the date sent, sender, recipient(s), subject or deliverable, method of transmission, whether the District received acknowledgment or feedback, and any recorded follow-up.

7. Existing records sufficient to show whether any agreed deliverable, remedy, or systemwide change was delayed because the District was awaiting OCR feedback, approval, direction, or contact.

This request seeks records as maintained by the District. It does not ask the District to create a new report, narrative, chronology, database, legal analysis, or compilation. If an existing record contains some but not all requested information, please produce the record in its existing form. If no responsive records exist for a category after a reasonable search, please say so in your response.

Please provide records electronically by email or download link. If you contend that any portion is exempt, please release all reasonably segregable nonexempt material and identify the specific exemption(s) and the basis for each withholding. Before incurring any charge, please contact me with an itemized estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Marina Villeneuve
